author: Thoughty2
description:
A solid, uninterrupted 8 hours of sleep is the dream, right? Well, not necessarily...

History professor Roger Ekirch discovered hundreds of references suggesting that, prior to the Industrial Revolution, people commonly slept in two chunks: a “first sleep” and a “second sleep”, with a few hours of wakefulness in between.

During this nocturnal intermission, people might pray, read, chat, do some chores, or even enjoy a bit of how’s-your-father before heading back to bed.

So if you regularly wake up at 3am, it might not be insomnia to blame. You might just be sleeping like your ancestors.

Although try telling that to your boss when you’re late for work…
title: Why Two Sleeps Might Be Better Than One
